approach: Add one reading check, `check_records_measure`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs` beside `check_history_fixture`. It has the same gate (`changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, surveys.rs:237) and fires on either of two triggers. (a) WORDS: the summary or a criterion names a records-computed measure by its real names: keep rule, planning cost, refusal rate(s), refusal count(s), refusal share, check duration(s), landing time(s), landed time, wasted work, `unlanded time spent`, `time spent per job`, the identifier `time_spent`, and throughput only in records phrases (throughput section, review, figure(s), measure(s), status). Bare `time spent` is not a trigger (finding 6). Matching is whole words on lowercase, whitespace-normalised text. Hyphens and underscores read as spaces for the phrase list; the identifier `time_spent` is matched on a hyphen-only form. (b) PATHS: a non-deleted deliverable is a module that computes figures: `crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs` (module doc lines 1-2: throughput and wasted work, check durations at :63, landed_jobs :472, time_spent :452, Throughput::compute :660) or `crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs` (module doc lines 1-2: planning cost, the keep rule). `crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs` is NOT a path trigger: it holds only record types (finding 5). A fired reading is accepted only if one Behavior criterion names `real records`, an independent source (`git log`, `history.json`, `commit times`, `recorded check durations`, `recorded durations`, `landing record timestamps`) and `expected range`. Otherwise the check bails naming the trigger and the missing parts. Criteria containing `newly refused` are not scanned for words, and the sentence `higher refusal rate is intended` is stripped after whitespace normalisation. The doc comment and the changelog state that code-health splits or moves of the two figure modules also need the criterion, because a moved figure can change (finding 7). One `step!` line goes in `refusing_check` after `check_history_fixture`; one reader rule line and one planner rule line state the rule.

decisions.choice: Answer findings 1-4: keep checks.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, briefs/reader.rs and briefs/planner.rs in the file list although the reading's deliverable list omits them. Nothing else outside the list is touched.
decisions.reason: Each is the only place the behavior can live, and I re-read each. checks.rs:518-547 holds `refusing_check`; its doc (checks.rs:510-514) says a new check is one `step!` line there and never a direct call. refusal_corpus.rs must gain a case where the new step refuses, or `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails and `cargo test` with it. briefs.rs only declares `mod planner; mod reader;` (briefs.rs:17-18), re-exports READING_RULES (briefs.rs:30) and holds the tests (from :1414), so the rule lines are built in briefs/reader.rs and briefs/planner.rs. Criterion 1 and the producer's report say so. The user has no other way to get the lines into the generated briefs.

The path corpus case is rebuilt on a status/throughput.rs deliverable. A new accepted case has records/throughput.rs as a deliverable and no measure word.

Commit 3a25c33 touched that file for DutyPass and HestiaSweep, so it is a false positive and is dropped as evidence and from the share estimate. The two remaining modules' docs say they compute figures. Words still catch status.rs refusal counts, which live in shared code (ReadingRuleStats, status.rs:185).

rejected.why: Misses a measure change such as 5724053 'refusal counts' (HISTORY.txt line 109) that names no listed phrase.

decisions.choice: Do not use bare `time spent` as a word trigger. Use `unlanded time spent`, `time spent per job` and the identifier `time_spent` instead, and add an accepted case for a CI-wait reading ('reduce time spent waiting for CI') (finding 6).
decisions.reason: Bare `time spent` is ordinary English. The measure it names is time_spent in status/throughput.rs:452, already covered by the path trigger and the identifier. `wasted work` stays: it is the section name in status/throughput.rs:1 and is not common phrasing. Because underscores read as spaces for phrases, `time_spent` is matched on a hyphen-only form so it is not confused with the English phrase.

rejected.option: Drop it and rely on path only
rejected.why: A reading about the figure written in words in another file would be missed; the narrowed phrases cost little.

decisions.choice: Code-health splits or moves of the two figure modules are refused like any other change to them: the doc comment and the CHANGELOG say so, and a corpus case 'measure-module-split-refactor' (summary says it moves code with no behavior change, deliverable status/throughput.rs, no real-records criterion) pins Refuse (finding 7).
decisions.reason: cf59590 (HISTORY.txt line 309) shows such splits happen. A move can change a figure, which is how both 2026-10-29 errors arose from small changes. An exemption needs summary parsing of 'no behavior change', which the lexical style of check_history_fixture (surveys.rs:320-321) avoids. The cost is one criterion, and the refusal text says it. A cheap fixture-free option for such jobs: a criterion running `status --snapshot` before and after against the same real range.

rejected.option: Exempt readings that declare a move
rejected.why: Needs negation and intent parsing and reopens the gap.

decisions.choice: Reader section: keep `assert!(section.len() < 3150)` and add no-growth against the measured baseline. The test comment says the bound is the <3150 section limit in briefs.rs (baseline 3045 recorded at briefs.rs:3555-3558), not the reader budget set (finding 9).
decisions.reason: BudgetSet in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs does not include READING_RULES, as the 'Prompt sets and budgets' system fact says, so '2 tokens left' refers to the always-loaded set. The section limit is the one that binds the new line. No-growth is kept as the conservative choice for the reading's 'replace or shorten' wording. The new line is at most 220 characters; existing entries are shortened by at least its length plus 3 bytes, keeping every pinned phrase. If that cannot fit, the producer stops and reports; it does not raise the limit.

rejected.why: The test would pass without meeting the criterion.

decisions.choice: Planner line: REAL_RECORDS_RULE is one line of at most 200 bytes, found once in the Report; the test asserts `report.len() <= REPORT_BASE + REAL_RECORDS_RULE.len() + 4`, REPORT_BASE measured with empty inputs before the change.
decisions.reason: 200 bytes is about 67 tokens, inside the planner's 95-token headroom; later growth fails the test.

decisions.choice: A criterion containing `newly refused` is skipped for word triggers, and `higher refusal rate is intended` is stripped after whitespace normalisation.
decisions.reason: The reader brief tells readers to write that declaration for every refusal rule; it must not trip another rule. Existing declared-intended tests (refusal_corpus.rs:2806, 2852, 2947) carry the words.

rejected.option: Strip only the literal sentence from raw text

decisions.choice: Independent sources accepted: git log, history.json, commit times, recorded check durations, recorded durations, landing record timestamps. The refusal text takes the example range from history.json commit times or landing record timestamps and presents `status --snapshot` only as the real output compared against that range.
decisions.reason: `status --snapshot` prints the code under change, so it cannot be the independent source. `git log` is in ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES (surveys.rs:561-567) and needs an `Environment:` assumption. `history.json` and `commit times` are not, and scan_segments breaks a token at an interior `.`, so that form needs no assumption; a test asserts it.

rejected.option: Only git log and recorded check durations
rejected.why: Forces an Environment assumption; the verifier has no git.

decisions.choice: One Behavior criterion must hold `real records`, an independent source and `expected range`. A reading that names a measure only to say it is unchanged is still refused, and a corpus case pins it.
decisions.reason: One criterion ties the real run to the independent range; a Content criterion runs nothing. The check is lexical (surveys.rs:320-321), and a nearby change can move a figure.

rejected.option: Accept the parts spread over several criteria
rejected.why: A real-records criterion could have no range.

decisions.choice: Stored readings that newly fail leave the drain queue until `athena go` or a re-read; no new drain test. This job's own accepted reading is among the newly refused (finding 8) and is counted in the share.
decisions.reason: drain.rs:114-124 and steward.rs:424 route stored readings through `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54), as for any failing check; drain.rs tests at :4406 pin that. Criterion 3 of this job's reading is a Behavior criterion naming 'landing time' with no real-records criterion and no 'newly refused', in a code reading, so the new check refuses it. The verification replay will therefore count at least this one reading, and it is in the estimate: about 7 HISTORY.txt subjects name these measures (lines 109, 441, 709, 1233, 1266, 1285, 1400) plus this job, so about 8 of 200 = 4%; 3% is the declared estimate (not measured). The replay at verification measures the real share, and the verifier should expect this job's own reading in the count.

rejected.option: Add a new cli drain test
rejected.why: It would re-test generic routing; the new part is the Refuse from check_reading_text.

demonstrations.method: A test modelled on `history_fixture_refusal_is_declared_intended` (refusal_corpus.rs:2919) reads the doc comment above `pub fn check_records_measure(` from the surveys source (via `reading_source()`, line 2673) and checks it, and calls `replay_declaration` on a criterion with the declaration.
demonstrations.observes: The doc comment holds 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.', 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', 'estimate', the 2026-10-29 figures 0.1 and 273.8 minutes, and a Limits paragraph (lexical; unchanged-measure and split readings still refused; status.rs refusal counts caught by words only). `replay_declaration` returns share Some(3).
demonstrations.fails_without: Missing declaration or limits make the needle assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration` and the source reader in refusal_corpus.rs (exists); the test is added by plan step 8. No double.

demonstrations.method: The same test collapses the whitespace of CHANGELOG.md (include_str!, as the existing declared-intended tests do) and checks the new item; the diff shows it under [Unreleased] / Changed.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus records_measure_refusal_is_declared_intended && git diff -U0 -- CHANGELOG.md
demonstrations.observes: The item names `reading::check_records_measure`, states the rule, cites landing time 0.1 and 273.8 minutes on 2026-10-29, gives the history.json commit-time example with `status --snapshot` as the output compared against it, says splits of the figure modules also need the criterion, and contains 'higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 3% of newly refused readings'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the item the changelog assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: CHANGELOG.md read with include_str! in refusal_corpus.rs; exists. No double.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks, then the corpus alone. New corpus cases: records-measure-change-on-fixtures-only-job-landing-time (Refuse), refusal-counts-status-from-5724053 (Refuse; summary 'Report per-rule reading refusal counts in status', deliverables as in HISTORY.txt lines 109-113), measure-module-path-no-measure-word (Refuse; deliverable crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs), measure-module-split-refactor (Refuse), records-measure-named-as-unchanged (Refuse), records-measure-change-with-real-records-range-history-json (Accept, no assumption), ...-git-log (Accept, Environment assumption), refusal-rate-declaration-wrapped-line (Accept), docs-reading-naming-landing-time (Accept), ci-drain-throughput-reading (Accept), ci-wait-time-spent-reading (Accept), records-throughput-record-types-no-measure-word (Accept; deliverable crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs). I did not run any of this and cite no result.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: All pass. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` finds check_records_measure refusing in the first case; `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` passes with the new tags; `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` passes. Existing cases keep their outcome: the measure phrases appear in refusal_corpus.rs only in declared-intended sentences, which are skipped.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new corpus case `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails; any broken existing reading test fails cargo test.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` called by the corpus harness `run(c)` with new `Case` values built by the existing `case(...)` helper, `repo_files` set as the history cases do. Plan step 7 adds them. No double.
